points: The trial ran from 10 a.m. on November 2 to 10 a.m. on November 3 and was livestreamed to an audience of more than two million viewers across online platforms.
Four of the six robots passed the final performance assessment.
The event marked the conclusion of AGIBOT’s AI WAVE technology showcase, launched on October 22.

title: How Rhoda AI is using video data to create generalized AI models for robots
summary: Rhoda AI offers a direct video action model, which it recently extended with mobile DVA, to enable robots to understand the physical world.
points: Rhoda pretrains its models on internet-scale video to build a strong prior on motion, physics, and physical interaction. | Source: Rhoda AI
Earlier this year, Rhoda AI emerged from 18 months of stealth with $450 million in Series A funding.
The company is working with customers in automotive, manufacturing, logistics, and e-commerce to deploy its direct video action, or DVA, model for robotics.

title: Robot Talk Episode 170 – Robots in the real world, with Daniela Shchegelskaya
summary: Claire chatted to Daniela Shchegelskaya from the University of Twente about getting robots to operate reliably in safety-critical environments. Daniela Shchegelskaya is an electronics and robotics eng
points: Daniela Shchegelskaya is an electronics and robotics engineer specialising in autonomous systems, control engineering, and Al-driven robotics for industrial and safety-critical environments.
She works on deploying real-world autonomous robots beyond lab conditions, focusing on reliability, connectivity, and system-level design.

At Elimpus, she works on the integration of Boston Dynamics’ Spot for inspections in live power substations, including autonomous navigation, network connectivity, remote diagnostics, data collection and system-level reliability.

title: Narwal builds robot vacuums to serve regional needs
summary: Narwal executives say they spent a decade in research and development and have tailored their household cleaning robots to local markets.
points: Robots have entered homes, but the path to consumer adoption has been long and winding. iRobot Corp. was the pioneer but entered bankruptcy proceedings late in 2025.
Narwal Robotics Corp. has spent a decade on research and development, testing 30 technical routes to self-cleaning robotic mops, and building a supply chain to retain cost control.

The company , which has offices in Shenzhen, China, and Covina, Calif., is looking to embodied intelligence to take home robots from the “iPod stage” to the “iPhone moment,” according to founder and CEO Junbin Zhang.
